description: Page counts per state per corpus tier. Not a suite output — verified by directly counting pages in the source PDFs with PyMuPDF, re-verified 2026-08-16 (see paper/results/task1_20260816/manifest.json -> corpus_pages_verified).
verification_command: python -c "import fitz; print(fitz.open(path).page_count)"  # run once per PDF under standards/
notes: CO has no single 'full' page count: the birth-to-8 document is 187pp, the 3-5-only document is 41pp; the _only_subset (10pp) and _trimmed (41pp) tiers both derive from the 3-5 document.

CO's _trimmed file is not trimmed at all: colorado_3_5_trimmed_2020.pdf (41pp) equals full_3_5 (41pp). The 187pp birth-to-8 file is the wider publication the Ages 3-5 band is drawn from (its TOC puts 'Ages 3-5' at p77), so CO's out-of-scope content is other AGE BANDS, not trimmed-away standards.
CA has no _trimmed tier — its full (68pp) PTKLF 'at a glance' document was cut directly to the 13pp _only_subset.
The held-out canary is NV-2023 (nevada_standards_2023_only_subset.pdf, multi-domain), not NV-SES-2025 (single-domain, too narrow for a generalization claim).
All current eval numbers in paper/results/task{1,2}_20260816/ are from the _only_subset tier only — no table anywhere in this paper may present them as full-document numbers (guardrail 1).

tier_definitions.full: The published PDF as downloaded, unmodified.
tier_definitions.trimmed: Non-standards matter removed — front matter, preamble, guiding-principles essays, appendices, acknowledgements. Retains 100% OF THE STANDARDS (confirmed 2026-08-31 by Emily, who performed the trimming). It reduces page count and therefore cost, NOT coverage: KY's 52pp of a 120pp publication is all of Kentucky's standards. Do not present a trimmed/full page ratio as a coverage fraction.
tier_definitions.only_subset: A genuine coverage reduction: ~1-2 domains per state, fully annotated, cheap to iterate on. This is the tier guardrail 3's 'favorable preprocessing' disclosure is about, and the tier every quality table uses.
